title: fix: limit community monitor probe load
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Sends one routine request per listed community model instead of 1–4 cost-weighted requests
- Keeps targeted confirmation probes and the four-hour image cadence unchanged
- Removes obsolete adaptive-budget allocation while preserving actual spend tracking

Checks:
- Biome
- `node --check operations/community-monitor/probe.mjs`
- localhost two-model fixture: 2 models, 2 requests

gist.headline: One bee per flower
gist.blurb: The community monitor now checks each listed model once per routine pass instead of buzzing back four times. Targeted follow-ups and the four-hour image rhythm stay right where they were.
gist.summary: Simplified the community-model monitor so each listed model receives one routine probe instead of 1–4 cost-weighted requests, while retaining targeted confirmation probes, spend tracking, and the four-hour image cadence.
gist.impact: Community model monitoring now creates a predictable one-request-per-model routine load without changing confirmation checks or scheduled image probes.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden inspector with a tiny clipboard, visiting one code-flower per pot in a cozy model garden rather than repeatedly checking the same plants. A small CRT monitor robot tracks a neat one-check-per-flower list, with a clock showing the unchanged four-hour image watering schedule.
